editorial_rules.publication_unit: Provider and brand-led landscape, with selected named products where a distinct buying need warrants a separate entry.
editorial_rules.primary_placement_rule: One logo placement per record, based on a documented in-scope role. This is editorial navigation, not an exhaustive capability boundary or ranking.
editorial_rules.secondary_capability_rule: Use sourced capability tags for overlaps. Missing tags mean not yet evidenced in this review, not absence of a capability. Use the same evidence standard for Trust.med and other providers.
editorial_rules.product_entry_rule: A separate product tile requires a documented product name, a distinct in-scope function and a linked provider or brand record. Parent/service provider tiles may coexist, but records are not counted as independent companies. Do not create extra tiles merely for editions, modules or aliases.
editorial_rules.product_catalog_limit: The current landscape is not a complete product-by-product catalog. EXODUS is an explicit migration-product entry; other product coverage will be assessed under the same rule.
editorial_rules.identity_rule: Preserve stable record IDs and baseline aliases internally. Publish parent or affiliation claims only with supporting evidence. A product logo is not evidence of IP ownership.
editorial_rules.evidence_rule: Supported means official evidence supports the described narrow role. Partial means a material identity, scope or availability question remains. Generic untested-performance caveats do not by themselves require partial status.
editorial_rules.availability_rule: A live web page or crawl date alone does not establish current sales, deployment or production readiness. Do not convert undocumented capabilities into confirmed capabilities.
editorial_rules.ai_rule: Badge only an identified customer-facing AI offering or AI connectivity capability, backed by an official source or attributed company information. Do not infer from company name or apply parent AI offerings automatically to every brand.

Manage product-event data and traceability workflows. EPCIS support is recorded separately when specifically evidenced.

Connect, exchange, transform and retain supply-chain data, and make it usable through reporting, analytics and AI-enabled access. Provider-specific capabilities are documented in the directory; other categories may overlap.
Exchange business messages and files. Native serial repositories or regulatory compliance are not assumed.
Connect applications and systems through APIs or integration tooling.
Manage and synchronize product or location reference data, distinct from serialized events.
Pharmaceutical pricing, eligibility or transaction exchange adjacent to product traceability.
Named tools that transfer, transform or reconcile historical serialization data between platforms. Consulting services remain in the services band.
Receive serialized product data and reconcile inbound or operational records.
ERP or inventory workflows incorporating serialized product handling; native and externally integrated capabilities must be distinguished.
Execute serialized warehouse movements, aggregation, rework or logistics events.
Verify product identifiers or investigate and resolve traceability exceptions; US and EU workflows are distinguished in details.
Establish trading-partner identity or credentials, distinct from product authentication.
Validate trading-partner licenses or provide licensing reference data.
Technology supplying medicines-verification systems; distinguish vendors from system operators.
Software for facility or business license requirements, applications and renewals. Adjacent to product traceability.
Advisory and planning services with relevant pharma or traceability evidence. Adjacent candidates are identified in the directory.
Implementation, integration or specialist operational services; named software is described separately.

Compliance-readiness support for pharmaceutical supply-chain participants and independent interoperability/conformance testing. Practice advisory, implementation validation, credential audits and protocol certification are distinguished in provider capabilities; inclusion does not imply regulatory approval.
Operators performing packaging or serialization services; not assumed to sell standalone software.

findings.title: Reconcile categories and evidence
findings.text: Primary placement is a navigation aid, not an exclusive capability boundary. Rename traceability data workflows to avoid implying universal EPCIS support; distinguish regulatory gateways from enterprise platforms; move licensing software into the technology layer; relate EXODUS to Jennason and AnkHero.

findings.title: Update the corporate families
findings.text: Antares Vision is now wholly owned by Crane NXT; rfxcel belongs within that group. Preserve these brands for product discovery, but aggregate them when counting independent competitors.

findings.title: Place PCE with Systech
findings.text: Systech acquired PCE in March 2024. Systech sits within Markem-Imaje / Dover. Older METTLER TOLEDO brochures still describe PCE, so the current METTLER TOLEDO entry is limited to pharmaceutical inspection evidence.

findings.title: Link brands without double-counting companies
findings.text: SEA Vision belongs to Marchesini Group. Syndigo acquired 1WorldSync. NNIT incorporated Excellis in January 2025, and SteriPack adopted the Ensera name. PRG describes LSPedia as a sister-company; the review does not assert a direct parent relationship.

findings.title: Represent breadth through capability tags
findings.text: ACG, OPTEL, Systech, Jekson Vision and other providers span several serialization layers. A primary placement is a navigation aid. Axway belongs in enterprise traceability as well as verification routing; services firms Ankhero, Jennason and VariTec also offer specialist software.

findings.title: Separate capture, authentication and verification
findings.text: Scanning hardware captures codes; physical authentication examines a product or package; DSCSA verification and EU FMD verification have different workflow contexts. QicScan is supported as a capture offering, while the SG Labs relationship still needs evidence.

findings.title: Distinguish integration from serialized event management
findings.text: EDI networks, APIs, product-data services and EPCIS repositories solve different problems. Pharmaceutical EDI evidence supports inclusion in the enabling layer without establishing a standalone serialization platform or end-to-end regulatory solution.

findings.title: Correct the managed-services implication
findings.text: Jennason explicitly excludes long-term serialization outsourcing and managed support. Its advisory, migration, implementation and software capabilities remain in scope. RSM remains an adjacent advisory candidate because the reviewed evidence does not establish a dedicated serialization service.

findings.title: Broaden the missing categories and providers
findings.text: Add medicines-verification infrastructure providers Solidsoft Reply and Tiga, plus evidence-backed packaging, authentication, labeling and services providers. GS1 and EMVO remain ecosystem context. EMVO directory candidates are flagged until their current commercial identity and offering can be established.
